title: Crossing Numbers of Knots on Closed Surfaces
summary: Let c(K;F) denote the surface crossing number of a knot K with respect to a closed connected surface F in S^3. We relate c(K;F) to the tunnel number t(K) and to the Heegaard deficiency delta(F)=g(M_1;F)+g(M_2;F)-g(F), where S^3=M_1 union_F M_2. The zero-crossing case gives a structural obstruction: if c(K;F)=0, then t(K) delta(F), then c(K;F) >= 2(t(K)-delta(F))+1. Thus the Heegaard deficiency of F measures the amount of tunnel complexity that can be absorbed by F without producing crossings.
